subject: Evaluation & MAP: security checkpoints + retention exception request
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluation & MAP: security checkpoints + retention exception request

Hi Alice — great to meet yesterday. As promised, here's a concise MAP for the evaluation sprint and the specific security/compliance items LedgerCorp asked us to clarify. Goal: keep the eval moving while we resolve a single retention carve-out request.

Proposed short MAP (kickoff week -> production pilot):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize DPA redlines and agree on retention exception scope
- Week 1: evidence intake (SOC 2 artifacts + SIG answers) and technical onboarding
- Week 2: smoke tests + canary traffic (hosted)
- Week 3: evaluate performance + finalize SLA baseline

Security/compliance asks (items LedgerCorp flagged):
1) SOC 2 snapshot: we can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II snapshot (Mar 2028). It covers typical infra/process controls; confirm whether LedgerCorp needs the full SOC 2 report or just the cover and control summary.
2) SIG/CAIQ: attached is our initial SIG answers workbook (SIG-answers-v1.xlsx). We'll complete any follow-ups you highlight.
3) DPA redlines: attached is our suggested counter-redline (DPA_redlines_Ledger_v2.docx). Key open item: LedgerCorp's requested 7-year retention for transaction derivatives — we think a scoped exception limited to anonymized logs + lawful retention purpose might bridge this.
4) Data residency & retention: default retention options are 90/365/indefinite archive. For regulated datasets LedgerCorp described, propose a special retention lane: 5 years active + encrypted archive for 2 additional years; full deletion upon contract termination unless legal hold.

Straight asks / next steps from LedgerCorp to unblock the MAP:
- Confirm whether SOC 2 cover + control summary is sufficient today, or if you require the full report and NDA.
- Mark up our DPA redlines with the minimum retention language you need (highlight by May 24).
- Any SIG follow-ups (we'll prioritize).
- Availability for a 30m alignment call Wed 5/23 10:00–10:30 PT?

Attaching: SOC2_snapshot_March2028.pdf (summary), DPA_redlines_Ledger_v2.docx, SIG-answers-v1.xlsx

Thanks — aiming to keep the eval on a two-week runway.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation & MAP: security checkpoints + retention exception request

Thanks for the clear MAP, Steph — copying internal owners to tighten the ask. A couple of internal notes before we send our legal-approved language back to Alice: 

- SOC 2: We should offer the SOC 2 cover + control summary first (no full report unless they return an NDA). Rachel, can you prepare the one-page control mapping for LedgerCorp's top three controls (data residency, encryption, incident mgmt)?
- DPA retention: Karthik, legal would prefer we avoid an indefinite archival commitment. For a regulated customer asking 7 years, a 5+2 encrypted-archive compromise is workable but we should include strict purpose limitation and encrypted-key escrow language.
- SIG workbook: I'll run the SIG answers through risk for any high impact gaps (esp. key management/KMS).

Action items: Rachel to draft control mapping by Tue EOD; Karthik to draft suggested DPA clause (5+2 model) and escalate any non-starters to Legal.

Kimberly
Director, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@ledgercorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ledgercorp.com
Date: 2028-05-21T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation & MAP: security checkpoints + retention exception request

Thanks, Stephanie — this is helpful and aligns with what the internal stakeholders asked for. A few quick clarifications before our alignment call: 

- SOC 2: the control summary is fine for now; Procurement will execute a mutual NDA if we need the full report.
- Retention carve-out: the business requirement for 7 years is driven by dispute-replay capability for legacy contracts; however, we can be flexible if data is strongly anonymized and stored encrypted. Would Redwood be open to key escrow with us holding the decryption key for the additional archive window?
- KMS/HSM: can you confirm whether keys are managed in an HSM-backed KMS and whether customer-managed keys are an option in the Private deployment? (This is important for our security team.)

We can do Wed 5/23 10:00 PT — Dave from Procurement will join. Also looping Procurement here: procurement@ledgercorp.com for PO/timing constraints.

Best,
Alice Jensen
Head of Platform Risk | LedgerCorp Financial
alice.jensen@ledgercorp.com | (202) 555-0134

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: LedgerCorp MAP — plan for Wed call & deliverables

Internal summary and plan ahead of Wed 5/23 10:00 PT (call with Alice + Procurement):

1) SOC 2 deliverable: Rachel to finalize the 1-page control mapping + confirm which SOC 2 attachments (system description, selected controls summary) we can share without NDA. Deadline: Tue 5/23 09:00 PT.
2) DPA redlines: Karthik to produce a clean clause implementing 5-years active + 2-year encrypted-archive with the following: purpose limitation, key escrow option, explicit deletion triggers, and audit logging requirements. Highlight any language that Legal will need to negotiate. Deadline: Tue 5/23 11:59 PT.
3) KMS/HSM response: I'll prepare a short runbook that explains: hosted default (Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys), dedicated/dplc options (customer-managed keys via supported KMS), and network constraints for Private. Send to Alice during the call.
4) SIG follow-ups: Kimberly to surface any high-impact SIG gaps; we'll triage into the MAP backlog.

Prep notes for the call: keep the meeting to 30m — focus on (a) DPA redline agreement in principle, (b) SOC 2 artifact handoff process (NDA vs summary), and (c) KMS option confirmation. If Procurement asks about PO cadence or committed capacity (Dedicated), we can provide a high-level estimate but defer fine numbers to the follow-up.

I'll upload the three attachments and the one-pager to the shared Drive link before the call.

— Steph
